source_metadata.exact_title: 21-Gene Assay to Inform Chemotherapy Benefit in Node-Positive Breast Cancer

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary objective was to assess the effect of chemotherapy on invasive disease-free survival and whether relative chemotherapy benefit increased with a higher recurrence score.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary objective was to assess the effect of chemotherapy on invasive disease–free survival and to assess whether a relative chemotherapy benefit would increase with a higher recurrence score.

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants were women at least 18 years old with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative, nodal stage N1, noninflammatory breast cancer without distant metastasis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We enrolled women who were at least 18 years of age and who had hormone-receptor–positive,11 HER2-negative,12 nodal stage N1, noninflammatory breast cancer without distant metastasis.

population.label: Eligible women with HR-positive/HER2-negative N1 noninflammatory breast cancer

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants had to have undergone primary surgery with sentinel-node biopsy or axillary lymph-node dissection and be eligible for taxane-, anthracycline-, or combined chemotherapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The participants had to have undergone primary surgery with sentinel-node biopsy or axillary lymph-node dissection and had to be eligible for a chemotherapy regimen that contained a taxane, an anthracycline, or both.

population.label: Surgically treated chemotherapy-eligible participants
inclusion_criteria: Sentinel-node biopsy or axillary lymph-node dissection
Eligible for taxane, anthracycline, or both

atoms.canonical_statement: Women with a recurrence score above 25 were ineligible; women with a recurrence score from 0 through 25 were invited to participate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Women with a recurrence score higher than 25 were ineligible for the trial, and it was recommended that they receive adjuvant chemoendocrine therapy. Women with a recurrence score of 0 to 25 were invited to participate in the trial.

atoms.canonical_statement: The intervention was adjuvant chemotherapy plus endocrine therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants who provided consent were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive chemoendocrine therapy or endocrine therapy only.

exposures.details: Adjuvant chemotherapy plus endocrine therapy (chemoendocrine therapy)

atoms.canonical_statement: The comparator was adjuvant endocrine therapy only.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants who provided consent were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive chemoendocrine therapy or endocrine therapy only.

exposures.details: Adjuvant endocrine therapy without assigned chemotherapy

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were randomized 1:1, stratified by recurrence score category (0-13 vs 14-25), menopausal status, and axillary surgery type.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants who provided consent were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive chemoendocrine therapy or endocrine therapy only. The stratification factors included the recurrence score (0 to 13 or 14 to 25), premenopausal or postmenopausal status, and type of axillary surgery (sentinel-node biopsy or axillary lymph-node dissection).

atoms.canonical_statement: Each participant was intended to be followed for 15 years after randomization.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each participant was to be followed for 15 years after randomization.

atoms.canonical_statement: Invasive disease-free survival was defined from randomization to first invasive recurrence, new invasive primary cancer, or death from any cause.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Invasive disease–free survival was defined as the time from the date of randomization to the date of a first invasive recurrence (local, regional, or distant), a new invasive primary cancer (breast cancer or another type of cancer), or death from any cause.

outcome.definition: Time from randomization to first invasive recurrence (local, regional, or distant), new invasive primary cancer, or death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: Distant relapse-free survival was defined as time to distant recurrence or death from any cause.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary end points included distant relapse–free survival (i.e., the time to distant recurrence or death from any cause) and overall survival.

outcome.definition: Time to distant recurrence or death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: Overall survival was a secondary endpoint.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary end points included distant relapse–free survival (i.e., the time to distant recurrence or death from any cause) and overall survival.

atoms.canonical_statement: Primary analyses used the intention-to-treat population of eligible participants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Analyses were conducted in the intention-to-treat population of eligible participants.

atoms.canonical_statement: Sensitivity analyses included per-protocol analyses among participants who accepted their treatment assignment at randomization.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Sensitivity analyses included per-protocol analyses involving the subgroup of participants who accepted their treatment assignment at the time of randomization.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary predictive analysis used a Cox model testing the interaction between treatment and continuous recurrence score, with menopausal status included.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In the primary analysis, we conducted tests for an interaction between chemotherapy and the continuous recurrence score with respect to invasive disease–free survival.

atoms.canonical_statement: A target sample of 5000 participants was estimated to provide 86% power to detect a predictive recurrence-score effect on chemotherapy benefit under the planned assumptions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We determined that a sample of 5000 participants would provide 86% power to detect a predictive effect of the recurrence score on a chemotherapy benefit, assuming an expected rate of invasive disease–free survival at 5 years of 92.4% in the overall trial population.

atoms.canonical_statement: Annual interim analyses were planned beginning after 24% of 832 expected invasive disease-free survival events, using an increasing alpha criterion preserving overall two-sided alpha 0.05.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Annual interim analyses were planned after 24% of the expected 832 events of invasive disease recurrence, new primary cancer, or death (the components of invasive disease-free survival) were observed; an increasing alpha criterion was used at each interim analysis so that the overall cumulative two-sided alpha level was 0.05.

atoms.canonical_statement: A total of 5018 eligible participants were included in baseline characteristics; 33.2% were premenopausal and 66.8% were postmenopausal.
At baseline, 65.3% of participants had one positive node, 25.2% had two, and 9.2% had three.
At baseline, 42.8% had recurrence scores 0-13 and 57.2% had scores 14-25.
Of 5083 randomized participants, 65 were later deemed ineligible and 34 withdrew consent after treatment assignment; the survival analysis population was 4984.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Between February 2011 and September 2017, a total of 5083 participants underwent randomization (Fig. 1). After randomization, 65 participants were deemed ineligible to participate in the trial because of close or positive surgical margins. A total of 34 participants withdrew consent after they received their treatment assignment; these participants were included in the assessment of baseline characteristics but were excluded from the survival analyses.

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment-assignment refusal was more frequent after assignment to chemoendocrine therapy: 402 participants (16.2%) versus 144 (5.8%) assigned to endocrine therapy only.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The intention-to-treat analysis included the participants who declined the assigned treatment, including 402 participants assigned to chemoendocrine therapy (16.2%) and 144 assigned to endocrine therapy (5.8%).

atoms.canonical_statement: Among those receiving chemotherapy, anthracycline plus taxane was the preferred regimen in premenopausal women (54%), while taxane plus cyclophosphamide was preferred in postmenopausal women (57%).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In the chemoendocrine group, the preferred chemotherapy regimen for premenopausal women was an anthracycline and a taxane (in 54%) and the preferred chemotherapy regimen for postmenopausal women was a taxane plus cyclophosphamide (in 57%).

atoms.canonical_statement: Within 12 months after randomization, 12.7% of premenopausal women had ovarian suppression: 6.3% in the chemoendocrine arm and 19.0% in the endocrine-only arm.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Within 12 months after randomization, 12.7% of the premenopausal women (6.3% in the chemoendocrine group and 19.0% in the endocrine-only group) had suppression of ovarian function (hereafter, ovarian suppression).

atoms.canonical_statement: At median follow-up of 5.3 years, 481 invasive disease-free survival events had occurred, representing 58% of the expected total events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: With a median follow-up of 5.3 years, the current analysis included 481 events of invasive disease recurrence, new primary cancer, or death (the components of invasive disease-free survival), which corresponded to 58% of the total expected events.

atoms.canonical_statement: Premenopausal subgroup estimates in Figure 3B consistently favored chemoendocrine therapy across number of positive nodes, nodal sampling type, and recurrence-score stratum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All the subgroups had a greater invasive disease–free survival benefit with chemoendocrine therapy than with endocrine therapy only (Fig. 3B). The hazard ratio was similar across the number of positive nodes, type of nodal sampling, and recurrence score (0 to 13 or 14 to 25) (Fig. 3B).

atoms.canonical_statement: Within premenopausal women, the estimated chemotherapy hazard ratio for invasive disease-free survival was 0.48 (95% CI 0.32-0.72) in women younger than 50 years and 0.98 in women 50 years or older; the age interaction was not statistically significant (P=0.06).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In premenopausal women who were 50 years of age or older, no chemotherapy benefit was observed (hazard ratio, 0.98); in women younger than 50 years of age, the hazard ratio was 0.48 (95% CI, 0.32 to 0.72), although the interaction was not significant (P = 0.06).

atoms.canonical_statement: Supplementary treatment-outcome analyses were explicitly exploratory and preliminary, did not adjust for multiplicity, and could lack power because of small numbers and nonrandomized post-randomization treatment selection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These analyses are exploratory and preliminary, do not adjust for multiplicity, and may lack power due to small numbers. Furthermore, selection of treatment type within the randomized arm depends on clinical factors and such factors are adjusted for in these analyses.

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment refusal was higher than expected and depended on recurrence score and assigned treatment, probably reducing power to detect a recurrence-score-by-chemotherapy interaction in the intention-to-treat analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The percentage of women who declined their assigned treatment was higher than expected and depended on both the recurrence score and the assigned treatment, so the power to find a significant interaction was probably reduced in the intention-to-treat analysis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial was not designed as a noninferiority trial, and overall survival data were not mature at this analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although the RxPONDER trial was not designed as a noninferiority trial, the curves in the postmenopausal group (3353 women) may be superimposed at 5-year follow-up and with close to 60% of the expected events already observed.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial could not determine whether the premenopausal chemotherapy benefit was attributable to direct cytotoxic effects, treatment-induced ovarian suppression, or both, and it was not designed to test replacement of chemotherapy by ovarian suppression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Whether a chemotherapy benefit in premenopausal women is due to both direct cytocidal effects and treatment-induced menopause remains unclear.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that postmenopausal women with one to three positive axillary nodes and recurrence score 0-25 could forgo adjuvant chemotherapy without compromising invasive disease-free or distant relapse-free survival.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We found that postmenopausal women with one to three positive axillary lymph nodes and a recurrence score of 0 to 25 were able to safely forgo adjuvant chemotherapy without compromising invasive disease–free survival and distant relapse–free survival.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that premenopausal women with one to three positive lymph nodes derived a significant chemotherapy benefit even at very low recurrence scores.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In contrast, premenopausal women with one to three positive lymph nodes had a significant benefit from chemotherapy, even with a very low recurrence score.
